They believe that a well-communicated risk is a risk halved, that shared understanding is the ultimate safeguard against chaos. This makes them invaluable in a crisis and insufferable in the planning room, where they will detain a project for hours dissecting a hypothetical.

This obsession, however, conceals a deep-seated insecurity. Kaelen mistakes the dense, Latinate armour of jargon for the substance of true rigour. They believe that if a warning is couched in complex, specialized language, it is inherently more valid. A simple statement like "the structure might collapse" becomes an indigestible monologue on "cumulative torsion fatigue" and "metastable load-bearing thresholds." In seeking to be powerfully clear, they become incomprehensible to all but a select few, creating the very communication breakdown they fear most. They are so busy demonstrating they are right that they fail to ensure the message is received, leaving dangers unaddressed while they admire the ornate scaffolding of their own warnings.

She will spend critical minutes parsing “multi-vector, cascading failure protocols” while the sirens blare, convinced her precise lexicon is the bedrock of safety. This blind spot leaves her shouting into a void of her own making, believing her impenetrable language is a shield, when it is, in fact, the very wall that isolates her. The greatest risk she fails to communicate is that of being utterly, precisely misunderstood.
